cases.contractUnderTest: src/engine/auras/aura-observations.ts stack semantics; src/engine/auras/aura-state.ts latestStackObservation and presenceAt
cases.purpose: On a stack-change event `stack` is the absolute resulting count after that event: the ascending chain reads 2, 3, ... 6; the descending chain's removebuffstack reading 1 proves the aura survived it (ACTIVE at that transition) and only the ordinary removebuff ends it (INACTIVE). Between transitions, with no retained coverage, presence is UNKNOWN.

rationale.text: A delta reading would need the first stack application to read 1, which never appears across 1,012 stack applications in two reports; an absolute-before reading would put a PRIOR count of 2 on an application that follows applybuff. The descending chain runs 1.18 s past its removebuffstack 1, which only the absolute-resulting reading allows.

limitations: A resulting count of ZERO appears in no capture and is not read as INACTIVE.
Presence between transitions needs coverage this slice does not retain; the UNKNOWN assertion pins that honestly.

cases.purpose: The resource snapshot attached to a costed COMPLETE cast is tagged PRE_COST with amount, max and cost preserved verbatim; an uncosted cast on the same actor stays EVENT_ASSOCIATED with a null cost. The finisher's 7/7 costing 7 is the cap-bounded falsifier of the post-cost reading.

rationale.text: amount == max while cost > 0 is decided from one event with no arithmetic: a post-cost reading would require holding max + cost, above the cap. The wider investigation behind the fixture found 126 cap-bounded falsifiers and zero counterexamples across 423 costed entries in two reports.

limitations: Establishes PRE_COST for costed COMPLETE casts only. resourcechange stays EVENT_ASSOCIATED because its evidence rests on same-timestamp adjacency.
Does not make the post-cost amount knowable.
gameVersion 1 / logVersion 17 only.

cases.purpose: Among all 42 of actor 19's casts before Q, the last COMPLETE Kingsbane is the one at 2,173,778 — an observation, needing no coverage — and the 24 melee autos and assorted abilities around it do not anchor it. The Vanish action likewise anchors at 2,176,120.

rationale.text: 'Most recent' is only meaningful when every candidate is present, which is why the slice widened the cast predicate to every actor-19 cast. EXACT with a value is an observation and needs no coverage; only the null (proven absence) branch is gated.

cases.purpose: The real Envenom at 2,090,898 plainly happened — it carries an Energy cost of 35 — yet its classResources omits the combo-point entry entirely. Asked for its combo points, the layer answers UNKNOWN / NO_OBSERVATION. Reading it as zero would manufacture the sharpest possible false rejection.

rationale.text: A second Envenom by the same actor 1,015 ms later carries t4: 6/7 cost 6, so the absence is a gap in the record, not a fact about the pool. NO_OBSERVATION is the layer's word for 'we hold the event and it carries no such snapshot'.

cases.purpose: Asked for actor 19's Energy 4.4 seconds after the last observation, the state layer returns that observation STALE with its own amount (250) and its own time — not a regenerated figure, not an interpolation, and not 250 minus the 35 the finisher cost.

rationale.text: The resource surface is an observation layer, not a simulator: no passive regeneration, no interpolation, no replay of a cost or a delta onto an earlier amount. STALE carries the age so a caller can see the gap it is being asked to tolerate.

cases.purpose: A sanitized slice whose SUBSET_SELECTION retained no coverage cannot prove that an actor never cast anything. Asked for actor 14's last completed cast over the whole window, the state layer must answer UNKNOWN for INSUFFICIENT_COVERAGE — never EXACT null, which would be a proven absence manufactured from trimming.

rationale.text: Absence claims are gated on COMPLETE coverage of the interval (state-result.ts). The harness grants coverage only from the artifact's retainedCoverage grants, which are empty because the transformation record says so. CLAUDE.md: partial event retrieval does NOT mean the player performed no events during the missing interval.

limitations: Pins the reason INSUFFICIENT_COVERAGE, which presumes the CASTS category is OBSERVABLE from captures. If the harness ever stopped granting capability to captures the reason would move to CAPABILITY_UNVERIFIED, and this case should fail so the change is reviewed.

cases.contractUnderTest: src/engine/auras/aura-state.ts presenceAt (carry-forward under retained AURAS coverage)
cases.purpose: With AURAS coverage retained for target 19 over the window, the Vanish buff applied at 2,176,120 is carried forward to the instant before the Garrote cast at 2,176,580: ACTIVE, anchored on the observed application, no duration invented anywhere. The removebuff that follows the cast on the same millisecond does not reach back.

rationale.text: The slice's predicate — every aura event targeting 19 or 21 in the interval, order preserved — is what makes the continuity claim honest; and at Q Warcraft Logs returns the cast BEFORE the removebuff, so BEFORE_EVENT at the cast excludes it.

cases.purpose: The Vanish BUFF (11327) on actor 19 is INACTIVE at the end of 2,176,580 because its removebuff is the last transition on that millisecond — an observation. Immediately before the Garrote cast on the same millisecond, presence would have to be carried forward from the 2,176,120 application, and this five-event slice retains no coverage to carry it, so the answer is UNKNOWN / INSUFFICIENT_COVERAGE. The kingsbane-cooldown and D2 slices retain that coverage and prove ACTIVE.

rationale.text: Carrying an anchor forward asserts that nothing in the track contradicted it in between, which needs complete coverage of the interval for the target. The legacy M5-C2 harness granted that coverage by declaration; the corpus grants only what the transformation record retains, and this slice's probe did not record whether every aura event on actor 19 in the interval was kept.

limitations: This is the corpus being stricter than the legacy M5-C2 harness, deliberately. The ACTIVE-at-Q fact is pinned on the two slices whose predicate retains AURAS coverage for target 19.

cases.purpose: Actor id 0 is a real id: nothing rules it out, so a cast with sourceID 0 binds a source actor 0 rather than reading as absence. Its targetID -1 is still the sentinel.

rationale.text: A truthiness check on the actor id would drop actor 0 into absence. The layer's rule is that only the verified -1 sentinel and a missing key mean 'no actor'; every other integer is an id.

limitations: Synthetic input: no committed capture contains actor 0.

cases.purpose: The largest committed slice — 1,083 events including a full combatantinfo with gear and a 76-entry talent tree — normalizes with every family recognised, nothing dropped, and captured order intact, including the eight events sharing Q's millisecond with the Garrote cast FIRST.

rationale.text: At Q the cast shares a timestamp with seven consequences and Warcraft Logs returns the cast first; the first C3a capture sorted by timestamp and got the DoT remainder wrong by 12 seconds. Order within a millisecond is evidence, and the normalizer must carry it through unchanged.

cases.contractUnderTest: src/wcl/retrieval-plan.ts (one dataType: All stream, no actor filter); event-normalizer.ts source reading
cases.purpose: Enemy-sourced events are ordinary events with a real source actor. The unfiltered All stream carries them, and normalization binds actor 160 as the source of each without special-casing hostility.

rationale.text: M3 ingests exactly one dataType: All stream with no actor filter because environment and enemy evidence is what actionability depends on; the source window held 202 boss-sourced events alongside 4,339 others, and this slice is four of them.

cases.purpose: Real enemy-environment damage carrying sourceID -1 normalizes to a null source with the NO_ACTOR_SENTINEL reason, and no ActorRef -1 is ever minted. The four events also share one timestamp, so the count check doubles as proof that equal timestamps are not collapsed.

rationale.text: The -1 sentinel contract is owned by the normalization layer and is evidence-backed: the mid-fight window capture carries 92 events with sourceID -1 and 117 with targetID -1, including environment damage with no stated source. Reading -1 as an actor id would mint a well-formed actor that exists nowhere in master data.

limitations: Says nothing about negative values other than -1; that is the derived case's job.
gameVersion 1 / logVersion 17 only.

cases.purpose: The pull window — the only committed evidence for the flattened resourceActor attachment — normalizes with every family recognised, and each attached snapshot binds to the side resourceActor names: 2 is the TARGET's snapshot (a boss's health on a player's damage event), 1 is the SOURCE's. An event with no resourceActor carries no attachment.

rationale.text: The capture established that resource snapshots are FLATTENED onto the event with resourceActor saying which side they describe (1 = source, 2 = target); there is no sourceResources/targetResources object. Attributing a target-side snapshot to the source would hand a player the boss's health.

cases.purpose: Every raw type in the mid-fight window is an evidence-backed contract; captured order and same-millisecond runs survive normalization; a begincast whose targetID is -1 gets a null target with the sentinel reason while its source stays a real actor carrying its sourceInstance (50, instance 28); and a removebuff carries SOURCE 11 and TARGET 18 read from the verified field names, never swapped.

rationale.text: supported-families.ts recognises only raw types that appear in a committed capture, and this slice is one of the two the registry cites. Direction is read from the verified field names (sourceID/targetID), which the captures established; a removebuff from 11 on 18 is 11's aura leaving 18, and nothing infers the reverse.

cases.purpose: A negative source id that is not the verified sentinel is recorded as UNUSABLE_VALUE — neither an actor nor a 'no actor' statement — while the untouched sentinel events in the same payload keep their NO_ACTOR_SENTINEL meaning.

rationale.text: No evidence supports generalising -1's meaning. The normalization layer therefore records an unobserved negative as something it cannot interpret, and refuses to build an actor from it. The artifact is DERIVED: the -5 is constructed, and the case claims only how the layer treats it, not that it occurs.

limitations: The mutated event was never observed; this is a rule-of-the-layer claim, not a capture claim.

cases.purpose: An event whose type string no evidence-backed contract recognises is preserved as an UNSUPPORTED_TYPE event and counted under its verbatim type string. It is not dropped, and it is not coerced into a known family.

rationale.text: Only evidence-backed types are contracted (supported-families.ts). Anything else must fail closed as explicitly unsupported rather than disappear, because a dropped event would read downstream as an event that never happened.

limitations: Synthetic input. Proves the path, not any real Warcraft Logs type.

cases.purpose: Identified as a Protection Paladin, the same actor over the same artifact yields SPEC_NOT_SUPPORTED on both transports — a well-formed document that says gameplay analysis was not attempted, identical on REST and MCP.

rationale.text: An unsupported specialization must not produce an empty report that reads as clean play. The public contract carries SPEC_NOT_SUPPORTED as its own status, with zero coverage and no authority.

cases.purpose: The single-fight analysis of actor 19 over the D2 corpus is one document on REST and on MCP (structuredContent and text), valid against the frozen public schema, ANALYZED, and publishing MATCH as AUTHORITY_COMPATIBLE_ONLY.

rationale.text: One composition root builds one runner, both adapters receive it, and both call the same projection. Parity is tested rather than argued because a second projection added to one adapter is exactly the kind of change nothing else would notice.

cases.purpose: A local encounter-context request (no external references) over the same fake ports is one document on REST and MCP, valid against the frozen schema, with the external-reference section reporting NOT_REQUESTED. No rankings transport is wired, so nothing external could have been contacted.

rationale.text: Encounter context composes the raid-night SERVICE through one port set; a deployment that never enables external references wires no ranking transport at all, and the document says so explicitly rather than by omission.

limitations: External-reference behaviour is not exercised: M9-B runs only what deterministic injected responses can support, and no rankings fixture is committed to the corpus.

cases.purpose: One raid-night request for one fight with one Assassination participant, through the real raid-night service over fake ports carrying the D2 corpus, is one document on REST and MCP with exactly one ANALYZED cell.

rationale.text: The raid-night service is the production path with only the three Warcraft Logs ports faked; the cell is the real M5 facade's output projected by the real M7 aggregator.

limitations: The orchestration fixture normalizes the D2 artifact under its own window and fans it per participant; parity for other artifacts is not supported by this executor.

cases.purpose: The real Deathmark at 2,172,777 is compared and refuses: UNKNOWN because cds[0]'s condition ends in target.time_to_die and fight_remains, which are PREDICTIVE and never bound. A ready major cooldown that was actually used does not become a rejection just because the authority could not resolve.

rationale.text: Predictive state must not be substituted with the actual fight end. The decisive blocker is the scan's earliest unresolved candidate; the cds[0] entry's own reason is asserted directly by the legacy regression.

requiredStateEvidence: the Deathmark cast at 2,172,777 as the usability proof
no binding for target.time_to_die or fight_remains (PREDICTIVE)

cases.purpose: The max-combo-point Envenom at 2,178,582 reaches spend[1] SELECTED in one world, but core_dot[0] Garrote is still an unresolved candidate ahead of it, so another world plays Garrote. The comparison stays UNKNOWN with DIVERGENT_WORLDS rather than picking the lower-priority entry.

rationale.text: An UNKNOWN higher-priority APL condition must never fall through to a confident lower-priority recommendation. Divergence is the honest answer and the corpus pins it as such.

requiredStateEvidence: the Envenom cast at 2,178,582 carrying 7 / 7 combo points PRE_COST
the unresolved core_dot[0] Garrote candidate ahead of spend

cases.purpose: Immediately before the Garrote cast at Q, actor 19's Garrote on target 21 has 5,746 ms remaining: (2,164,326 + 18,000) - 2,176,580. The anchor is actor 19's own application, not actor 13's independent Garrote at 2,172,232, and not the re-application the cast itself causes.

rationale.text: The 18,000 ms duration is the pinned SIMC_DBC_ROGUE_DOT_DURATIONS dataset; the anchor is observed. Mistaking actor 13's application yields 13.652 s and the post-decision re-application yields 18.000 s — both plausible, only one right, and the slice contains both wrong answers so the derivation has to reject them.

requiredStateEvidence: every aura event targeting 19 or 21 in [2,164,325 .. 2,176,581], order preserved
the Garrote cast at 2,176,580 preceding its own removedebuff/applydebuff

cases.purpose: Actor 13's Envenom at 3 of 7 combo points is REJECTED: the spend gate is false under both Darkest Night resolutions. No replacement action is named — the globally ideal action stays UNKNOWN — and the rejection rests on the cast's own PRE_COST snapshot.

rationale.text: The pinned spend call condition is `!buff.darkest_night.up&combo_points>=5|buff.darkest_night.up&combo_points.deficit=0`; 3 < 5 and 3 != 7 fail it in every world. The observed 3/7 cost 3 is a cap-bounded PRE_COST observation on the cast itself.

requiredStateEvidence: the Envenom cast at 2,150,252 carrying classResources type 4: 3 / 7 cost 3

limitations: A rejection is not a coaching verdict; nothing here says what should have been cast.

cases.purpose: With no authority resolvable, the facade reports AUTHORITY_NOT_AVAILABLE and evaluates nothing — including the Garrote at Q that MATCHes under the pinned artifact. A missing standard is NO_AUTHORITY_AVAILABLE, never UNKNOWN and never REJECTED.

rationale.text: NO_AUTHORITY_AVAILABLE and UNKNOWN are semantically distinct and neither may produce a player-failure finding. The facade models 'no authority' only when the caller says so explicitly.

cases.purpose: The real post-Vanish Garrote at Q is the one resolved comparison on the D2 corpus: MATCH at EXACT_ENTRY precision on the garrote token, with no M5-A rejection. MATCH means the pinned authority's selection was compatible with the observed action — verification of an observed decision, not a prediction and not an endorsement.

rationale.text: Stealth from Vanish makes cds[5]'s !stealthed.rogue FALSE so the unsupported vanish list is never entered; the Garrote DoT anchor makes core_dot[0]'s remainder term derivable; and the observed cast proves usability. Under the pinned artifact simc-33622e9d-1 that selects garrote at core_dot[0] in every enumerated world.

requiredStateEvidence: Vanish buff 11327 ACTIVE at Q from the observed applybuff at 2,176,120
Garrote remains 5,746 ms from the 2,164,326 anchor
Kingsbane cooldown from the observed cast at 2,173,778
the observed Garrote execution at Q as the usability proof

limitations: MATCH = AUTHORITY_COMPATIBLE_ONLY. The positive usability came from the observed execution, so this does not claim the selection would have held beforehand.

cases.purpose: Asked to analyze actor 19 as paladin/protection, the facade returns SPEC_NOT_SUPPORTED before any Assassination rule runs. Protection Paladin remains explicitly unsupported until M10, and an unsupported spec never produces a decision list that could read as clean play.

rationale.text: The facade requires the caller's resolved specialization and checks it first; no default and no inference. A wrong spec must not fall through into Assassination rules.

cases.purpose: Actor 19's real build: improved_ambush is NOT_SELECTED because node 90692 carries a different entry (Tight Spender); shrouded_suffocation is SELECTED by its own entry 112669; blindside is UNKNOWN because its node is absent from the tree, and absence is never read as 'not taken'.

rationale.text: A node-presence rule would invert improved_ambush. Only two outcomes are decisive and both rest on an entry that IS present: the talent's own entry (SELECTED) or a different entry occupying its node (NOT_SELECTED). Missing talent data does not mean talent=false.

cases.purpose: The paginator requests page 2 at exactly the nextPageTimestamp page 1 returned (1500, no offset), stops on the terminal page, reports COMPLETE, and retrieves 4 events although two of them are identical in every observable field.

rationale.text: The paginator's three rules: the cursor is passed back VERBATIM as the next startTime because the schema documents it as exactly that; nothing is deduplicated because multiple legitimate events can share every field; there is no page-level retry.

limitations: Synthetic pages. A real report's page boundary has not been captured into the corpus.

cases.purpose: When page 2 carries data: null, the stream ends PARTIAL with MALFORMED_PAGE, the 2 events of page 1 are kept, and nothing is retried.

rationale.text: Every abnormal ending preserves what was already retrieved and records why it stopped. A failed page never becomes an empty period, which is the rule that keeps a 30-second retrieval gap from becoming 'you were idle for 30 seconds'.

cases.purpose: A ReportEventPaginator whose data is null decodes to MALFORMED_PAGINATOR. 'We could not read your events' must never become 'you produced no events'.

rationale.text: The decoder owns the classification and documents it in place: data: JSON is nullable upstream, and a null or non-array payload is a malformed page, never an empty one.

limitations: Exercises the decoder over a decoded data object, not a raw HTTP body; transport-level parsing failures are a separate boundary.
